title: Shader Forge — Live GLSL Studio
description: Write WebGL fragment shaders live, auto-generate sliders from comments, then export PNG, WebM or a share link.
concept: A full fragment-shader workbench in one file. Type GLSL and it recompiles as you go, with errors mapped back to your own line numbers and marked in the gutter. Any line like //@param gain 0 2 0.5 becomes a real uniform plus a live slider, and //@color tint #ff0066 becomes a vec3 with a colour picker. Nine presets — plasma, voronoi, clouds, a raymarched blob, truchet, kaleidoscope, metaballs, a warp tunnel and a starfield — give you something beautiful to take apart, and you can save sketches to your browser, grab a PNG, record the canvas to WebM, or pack the whole shader into a URL.
features: Live GLSL editor with syntax highlighting, line gutter and debounced recompile
Compile errors remapped to user line numbers and flagged in the gutter
Auto-generated parameter UI from //@param and //@color pragmas
Nine hand-written presets spanning 2D noise, tiling and raymarching
Shared prelude: rot, hash11/21/22, vnoise, fbm, pal, PI/TAU
PNG frame export and live WebM recording via MediaRecorder
Sketch library with thumbnails in localStorage, plus .glsl download
Shareable URL hash that packs the entire shader source
Pointer/touch drives u_mouse; play, pause and time reset

interaction.mouse: Move over the canvas to drive the u_mouse uniform; drag sliders to retune uniforms live.
interaction.click: Pick a preset, collapse the parameter dock, save a sketch, or export PNG / WebM / share link.
interaction.touch: Tap and drag the canvas to steer u_mouse; the toolbar scrolls horizontally and the code pane sits below.
interaction.keyboard: Space plays/pauses, Ctrl/Cmd+S saves a sketch, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter forces a recompile, Tab indents, Esc closes help.
